'''Andris Ambainis''' (born 18 January 1975)<ref name="lza" /> is a Latvian [[computer scientist]] active in the fields of [[Quantum information|quantum information theory]] and [[Quantum computer|quantum computing]].

==Education and career==
Ambainis has held past positions at the [[Institute for Advanced Study]] at [[Princeton, New Jersey]]<ref>{{Cite web |date=2019-12-09 |title=Andris Ambainis - Scholars {{!}} Institute for Advanced Study |url=https://www.ias.edu/scholars/andris-ambainis |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=www.ias.edu |language=en}}</ref> and the [[Institute for Quantum Computing]] at the [[University of Waterloo]]. He is currently a professor in the Faculty of Computing at the [[University of Latvia]].

He received a [[Bachelor's degree|Bachelors]] (1996), [[Master's degree|Masters]] (1997), and [[Doctorate]] (1997) in Computer Science from the University of Latvia, as well as a PhD (2001) from the [[University of California, Berkeley]].<ref name="lza">[http://www.lza.lv/scientists/ambainisa.htm Andris Ambainis' page] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140521031325/http://www.lza.lv/scientists/ambainisa.htm |date=2014-05-21 }} at the [[Latvian Academy of Sciences]].</ref>

==Contributions==
Ambainis has contributed extensively to quantum information processing and foundations of [[quantum mechanics]], mostly through his work on [[quantum walk]]s and lower bounds for [[Decision tree model#Quantum decision tree|quantum query complexity]].

==Recognition==
In 1991 he received a perfect score and gold medal at the [[International Mathematical Olympiad]].<ref>{{IMO results|id=2712}}.</ref> He won an [[Sloan Fellowship|Alfred P. Sloan Fellowship]] in 2008.<ref>{{Cite web |date=25 February 2008 |title=Fellowship Awarded to IQC Professor Andris Ambainis |url=http://iqc.uwaterloo.ca/news-events/archive/fellowship-awarded-to-iqc-professor-andris-ambainis |archive-url=https://wayback.archive-it.org/all/20110204131104/http://iqc.uwaterloo.ca/news-events/archive/fellowship-awarded-to-iqc-professor-andris-ambainis |archive-date=2011-02-04 |access-date=2024-12-11 |website=IQC.ca}}</ref> Ambainis was an invited speaker at the 2018 [[International Congress of Mathematicians]]{{r|icm}}, speaking on mathematical aspects of computer science.
